sessions.title: Tidepool Timekeepers Lab Clock
sessions.sessionFit: 32-minute adult-led after-school story club session for a table group that needs a calm opening, short draft, and optional read-back.
sessions.directorSetup: Print one page per writer, place pencils and three tide-card slips on each table, and set a front table as the pretend lab station.
sessions.kidDirection: Choose a tide time, add two careful lab details, and write a short note that helps the next timekeeper understand the order.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask the site lead to point writers toward time words, measured details, and one clear next step for the lab team.

pageSections.heading: Lab Clock
lines: The first tide time on the lab card is ____________________.
The next pool to check should be ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Observation Order
lines: Last, the tide note should explain ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Field Note
lines: One word that shows the order is ____________________.
My final tidepool lab note says ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: The time-order detail I can share with the club is ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: One observation I made clearer today was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: For a quiet version, number the tide cards and write the first note about ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one sequencing observations by time detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Plan
sessions.sessionFit: 35-minute after-school story club table block for a maker-style group that can sketch first and draft second.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the garden page, set out pencils and green or gray colored pencils, and draw three harmless gear shapes on the room board.
sessions.kidDirection: Invent a greenhouse gear, explain what it helps, and write the small adjustment that makes the garden schedule clearer.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Invite the site lead to ask what the gear helps, what gets confusing, and which gentle fix belongs in the next sentence.

pageSections.heading: Gear Idea
lines: The greenhouse gear is shaped like ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Schedule Problem
lines: The gear turns too early near ____________________.
The plant label that needs a clearer time is ____________________.
The helper notices the mix-up when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Design Fix
lines: The reason this helps the garden is ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: The design choice I can share with the club is ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: One exact garden word I used today was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: For a quiet version, sketch the gear first and label ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one explaining a helpful design choice detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Pantry Measurement Mystery Chart
sessions.sessionFit: 30-minute adult-led after-school club session for snack-table energy, quick evidence sorting, and a short explanation paragraph.
sessions.directorSetup: Print one pantry chart per writer, place pencils beside three recipe clue slips, and use a room board for a simple before-and-after chart.
sessions.kidDirection: Pick a pantry clue, compare the recipe notes, and write what changed in the muffin chart.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask the site lead to guide writers from guess words toward evidence words such as because, changed, and compared.

pageSections.heading: Cause Check

sessions.wrapUpLine: One cause-and-effect sentence I improved was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: For a quiet version, circle one recipe clue and finish ____________________.

sessions.title: Rain Gauge Railway Route
sessions.clubSkill: Using map words in a story route
sessions.sessionFit: 33-minute after-school story club session for a weather-themed table, with map planning before independent writing.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the railway route page, place pencils at each seat, and tape three pretend station labels to the tables in the room.
sessions.kidDirection: Choose the railway stops, add rain-gauge details, and write a route note that moves from start to finish.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Prompt the site lead to ask for direction words, one measurement detail, and a final station that makes sense.

sessions.title: Seed Library Map Room Card
sessions.clubSkill: Connecting setting details to next action
sessions.sessionFit: 36-minute adult-led after-school story club session for a steady table group that can sort cards and draft a return note.
sessions.directorSetup: Print seed-map pages, stack three blank packet cards per table, and set up pencils with one folded pretend map at the center.
sessions.kidDirection: Choose a seed packet, add a map-room clue, and write the next action for the catalog helper.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Have the site lead ask how the setting clue changes what the helper should do next.

sessions.title: Moss Message Observatory Note
sessions.sessionFit: 31-minute after-school story club session for a quiet table, useful when the group needs slower observation and descriptive writing.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the observatory page, set out pencils and green color swatches, and make a calm room corner for silent sketching before writing.
sessions.kidDirection: Choose a moss pattern, describe its color and texture, and write a field note for the observatory shelf.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask the site lead to help writers name what can be seen, felt, or measured in the pretend notebook scene.
